districts.name: Dotonbori
districts.fact: Dotonbori is Osaka's entertainment district — the neon-lit canal, giant mechanical signs (the Glico Running Man, the giant crab), and endless street food. It's the heart of Osaka's 'kuidaore' (eat until you drop) culture.
districts.budget: Free to walk, ¥1000-3000 for food crawl
districts.tips: Go at night when the neon is brightest. Try takoyaki from the street stalls — the ones with the longest lines are the best.

districts.name: Osaka Castle
districts.fact: Osaka Castle is one of Japan's most famous landmarks. Built in 1583 by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, the current structure was rebuilt in 1931. The museum inside has samurai armor and historical exhibits.
districts.tips: Go early to avoid crowds. The park around the castle is free and beautiful during cherry blossom season.

districts.name: Shinsaibashi
districts.fact: Shinsaibashi is Osaka's premier shopping district — a covered arcade stretching 600 meters with everything from luxury brands to quirky local shops. It connects directly to Dotonbori.
districts.tips: The covered arcade means you can shop rain or shine. Look for the side streets — they have the best hidden cafes and vintage shops.

districts.name: Universal Studios Japan
districts.fact: Universal Studios Japan is one of the most popular theme parks in Asia. Super Nintendo World opened in 2021 with a real-life Mario Kart ride. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is also here.
districts.tips: Buy express passes in advance — regular lines can be 2+ hours. Super Nintendo World requires a timed entry ticket even with admission.

districts.name: Kuromon Market
districts.fact: Kuromon Ichiba Market is Osaka's 'Kitchen of the Gods' — a 580-meter market street with 150+ shops selling fresh seafood, wagyu beef, and street food. It's been operating for over 100 years.
districts.tips: Go hungry. Must-try: grilled scallops, wagyu skewers, takoyaki, and fresh uni. Cash only at most stalls.

districts.name: Tsutenkaku Tower
districts.fact: Tsutenkaku Tower is Osaka's iconic 103-meter tower in the Shinsekai district. The surrounding area is old-school Osaka — retro arcades, pachinko parlors, and kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) on every corner.
districts.tips: The Billiken statue at the top is considered a good luck charm — rub its feet for good fortune. The view at sunset is spectacular.

food.name: Takoyaki
food.description: Octopus-filled batter balls topped with sauce, mayo, and bonito flakes. Osaka's signature street food — crispy outside, molten inside.

food.name: Okonomiyaki
food.description: Savory pancake with cabbage, meat/seafood, and toppings. Osaka-style is mixed together before cooking (vs Hiroshima-style layered).

food.name: Kushikatsu
food.description: Deep-fried skewers of meat, seafood, and vegetables. The rule: dip only once in the shared sauce! Double-dipping is a faux pas.

food.name: Ramen
food.description: Osaka is known for tonkotsu (pork bone) ramen. The broth is rich, creamy, and simmered for hours.

food.name: Yakiniku
food.description: Japanese BBQ where you grill premium beef at your table. Osaka has some of the best yakiniku in Japan.

food.name: Fugu
food.description: Blowfish — a delicacy in Osaka. Only licensed chefs can prepare it. The poison is removed, leaving a mild, translucent fish.
